crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Routing Across Automated Market Makers
children.blurb: Routing across automated market makers is the practice of finding and executing a trade path through one or more on-chain liquidity pools to get a desired asset at a better effective price than a single pool would offer.

children.name: Yield Strategies in Smart Contracts
children.blurb: Yield strategies in smart contracts cover onchain methods for earning a return on crypto assets by placing them into decentralised finance protocols.

children.name: On-Chain Forensics
children.blurb: On-chain forensics is the practice of tracing activity on public blockchains to identify who moved what, when, and why.

children.name: Stablecoin Stress Testing
children.blurb: Stablecoin stress testing is the practice of simulating severe but plausible market conditions to see whether a stablecoin can hold its peg and meet redemptions.

children.name: Governance Token Outcomes
children.blurb: Governance token outcomes refers to the measurable results of holding and using tokens that confer voting rights in decentralized protocols, including price performance, voting participation, treasury allocation, and protocol changes.

sections.body: Artificial intelligence in crypto markets and decentralised finance is mostly applied to execution, allocation, monitoring, and simulation. Routing across automated market makers uses algorithms to split a trade across pools and venues, aiming to reduce slippage and gas costs. Yield strategies in smart contracts use agents and optimisers to move capital between lending markets, liquidity pools, and structured products. On-chain forensics applies clustering, graph analysis, and anomaly detection to trace funds and flag suspicious activity. Stablecoin stress testing simulates redemption pressure, collateral shocks, and liquidity gaps to see where a peg might break. Governance token outcomes are studied with models of voting, delegation, and proposal incentives.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Basic routing and yield aggregation work in production, and address clustering is a standard forensic technique. What is not solved includes adversarial behaviour, maximal extractable value, cross-chain fragmentation, oracle failure, and the reflexivity of markets that react to the models watching them. Stress tests are only as good as their assumptions, and a simulated run does not prove a stablecoin will survive a real redemption wave. Governance token analysis often struggles with low voter turnout, concentrated holdings, and informal deals that never appear on chain. Regulatory treatment remains unsettled, and the site's 219 compliance and regulation pages show how much of the work is documentation, controls, and legal interpretation rather than prediction. AI cannot guarantee returns or replace audits, and it cannot resolve the legal status of a token or protocol.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section fit together as a chain from execution to risk to oversight. Routing Across Automated Market Makers is the place to start for how trades are split and settled across pools. Yield Strategies in Smart Contracts follows the capital after execution, covering lending, liquidity provision, and the risks that come with chasing returns. On-Chain Forensics covers the tracing and compliance side, including how investigators cluster addresses and follow funds. Stablecoin Stress Testing looks at the systemic end, where a single peg failure can spread through collateral and redemption channels. Governance Token Outcomes examines the incentive layer, where voting, delegation, and proposal design shape what protocols actually do.
